en: used to say that someone could have done something if a condition had been satisfied
used to describe an ability or opportunity that would have existed in a different past situation
used to describe a specific achievement that would have been possible with sufficient help, time, or resources
used in the negative to say that an action would have been impossible under particular conditions

nuance.ja: would have been able to は、過去の事実に反する条件のもとで存在したはずの能力・可能性を表す。通常は if＋過去完了を伴う仮定法過去完了の結果節で使われる。If I had had more time, I would have been able to finish. は、実際には時間が足りず、完成できなかったことを示す。could have finished でも近い意味を表せるが、could have done は『実際には使わなかった機会』や『ひょっとすると～した』という推測にもなる。would have been able to は、仮定条件から生じる能力という意味がより明確で、曖昧さが少ない。
nuance.en: Would have been able to describes an ability or possibility that would have existed under a counterfactual past condition. It commonly appears in the result clause of a third conditional with if plus the past perfect. If I had had more time, I would have been able to finish implies that I did not have enough time and did not finish. Could have finished can express a similar idea, but could have also describes unused opportunities or uncertain past possibilities. Would have been able to more explicitly identifies ability as the hypothetical result of a condition.

ja: I would have been able to finish if I had had more time.：もっと時間があれば、完成できただろう。
I could have finished.：完成することもできた・完成した可能性もある。
I was able to finish.：実際に完成することができた。
I would be able to finish.：条件が整えば、完成できるだろう。
I wouldn't have been able to finish without her.：彼女なしでは完成できなかっただろう。
couldn't have finished：完成できたはずがない・完成する能力がなかった。
would have managed to finish：何とか完成できただろう。困難の克服を強調。
en: I would have been able to finish if I had had more time describes counterfactual past ability.
I could have finished can describe either an unused opportunity or a possible past event.
I was able to finish states that the achievement actually occurred.
I would be able to finish describes ability under a present or future condition.
I wouldn't have been able to finish without her describes dependence on her help.
couldn't have finished can express either impossibility or lack of ability.
would have managed to finish emphasizes successful completion despite difficulty.

etymology.ja: would は will の過去形に由来し、古英語 wolde にさかのぼる。完了形 have been に able to を続けることで、過去のある条件下で成立したはずの能力を表す。able は古フランス語 able・habile を経て、ラテン語 habilis『扱いやすい、適した、能力のある』に由来し、habere『持つ』と関係する。
etymology.en: Would developed as the past form of will and goes back to Old English wolde. Combined with the perfect have been and able to, it describes an ability that would have existed under a past condition. Able came through Old French able or habile from Latin habilis, meaning suitable, manageable, or capable, and is related to habere, meaning to have.

note.ja: 過去に～することが可能だった。未使用の機会・反実仮想・過去の推測など、より広い意味を持つ。
note.en: Expresses past possibility and can describe an unused opportunity, a counterfactual result, or an uncertain past event.

note.ja: 特定の条件下なら、困難を乗り越えて何とか～できただろう。
note.en: Says that someone would have succeeded despite difficulty under particular conditions.

note.ja: 努力すれば何とか～できた可能性がある。能力と困難の克服を表す。
note.en: Suggests that successful completion despite difficulty was possible.

note.en: Describes an opportunity that would have existed, emphasizing opportunity rather than ability.

en: used to say that an opportunity would have existed if circumstances had been different
used to describe a chance to act or gain an experience that was not actually available
used to say that a particular event would have created an opportunity to do something
used in the negative to say that no such opportunity would have existed

nuance.ja: would have had the opportunity to は、過去の反実仮想において『行動するための機会・状況が与えられただろう』ことを表す。実際にその行為を実行できたか、また実行したかまでは示さない。would have been able to は能力または実行可能性、would have had the opportunity to は外部から与えられる機会に重点がある。could have done はより簡潔だが、未使用の機会、能力、過去の推測など複数の意味を持つため、この表現のほうが『機会』を明確にできる。やや長く形式的なので、日常会話では would have had a chance to もよく使われる。
nuance.en: Would have had the opportunity to describes an opportunity that would have existed in a counterfactual past situation. It does not itself establish whether the person had the ability to perform the action or whether they would actually have chosen to do it. Would have been able to emphasizes ability or practical possibility, whereas would have had the opportunity to emphasizes access to a favorable occasion or circumstance. Could have done is shorter but can express ability, unused opportunity, or uncertain past possibility. The present construction is relatively formal; would have had a chance to is common in conversation.

ja: I would have had the opportunity to meet her.：条件が整えば、彼女に会う機会を得られていただろう。
I would have been able to meet her.：条件が整えば、彼女に会うことが可能だっただろう。
I could have met her.：彼女に会うこともできた・会った可能性もある。
I had the opportunity to meet her.：実際に彼女に会う機会があった。
I would have had a chance to meet her.：彼女に会う機会があっただろう。より口語的。
I would have met her.：条件が整えば、実際に彼女に会っていただろう。
I missed the opportunity to meet her.：彼女に会う機会を逃した。
en: I would have had the opportunity to meet her says that an opportunity would have existed.
I would have been able to meet her emphasizes practical ability or possibility.
I could have met her can describe an unused opportunity or a possible past event.
I had the opportunity to meet her states that the opportunity actually existed.
I would have had a chance to meet her is the more conversational version.
I would have met her predicts that the meeting itself would actually have occurred.
I missed the opportunity to meet her says that an available opportunity was not used.

etymology.ja: opportunity は古フランス語 opportunité を経て、ラテン語 opportunitas『好都合、適切な時機』に由来する。これは opportunus『都合のよい、好機を与える』から派生した語。opportunus は伝統的に ob portum『港の方向へ』と関連づけられ、船を港へ運ぶ好都合な風のイメージから、望ましい機会・好機という意味が発達したと説明される。
etymology.en: Opportunity came through Old French opportunité from Latin opportunitas, meaning fitness, convenience, or a favorable occasion, derived from opportunus, meaning suitable or favorable. Opportunus has traditionally been associated with ob portum, toward the harbor, evoking a favorable wind carrying a ship toward port, although the precise historical formation is not entirely certain.

nuance.ja: would have had a chance to は、過去の反実仮想において『～する機会があっただろう』と述べる、自然で会話的な表現。would have had the opportunity to とほぼ同義だが、こちらのほうが短く口語的。have a chance to do の chance は通常『機会』を表す。一方、have a chance of doing は『～する可能性がある』という確率の意味になりやすい。したがって I would have had a chance to meet her. は『会う機会があっただろう』、I would have had a better chance of winning. は『勝つ可能性がより高かっただろう』となる。
nuance.en: Would have had a chance to is a natural conversational way of describing an opportunity that would have existed in a counterfactual past situation. It is nearly equivalent to would have had the opportunity to but is shorter and less formal. In have a chance to do, chance usually means an opportunity. By contrast, have a chance of doing commonly expresses probability. Thus, I would have had a chance to meet her concerns an opportunity, while I would have had a better chance of winning concerns the probability of success.

ja: I would have had a chance to meet her.：彼女に会う機会があっただろう。
I would have had the opportunity to meet her.：彼女に会う機会を得られていただろう。より形式的。
I would have had a better chance of winning.：勝つ可能性がより高かっただろう。
I would have been able to meet her.：彼女に会うことが可能だっただろう。
I could have met her.：彼女に会うこともできた・会った可能性もある。
I had a chance to meet her.：実際に彼女に会う機会があった。
I missed my chance to meet her.：彼女に会う機会を逃した。
en: I would have had a chance to meet her describes an opportunity that would have existed.
I would have had the opportunity to meet her is the more formal version.
I would have had a better chance of winning concerns the probability of winning.
I would have been able to meet her emphasizes practical ability or possibility.
I could have met her can describe an unused opportunity or a possible past event.
I had a chance to meet her states that the opportunity actually existed.
I missed my chance to meet her says that an available opportunity was lost.

etymology.ja: chance は古フランス語 cheance『偶然、出来事、運』を経て、俗ラテン語 cadentia『落ちること、起こること』に由来し、ラテン語 cadere『落ちる』と関係する。もとは『偶然降りかかる出来事』を指し、そこから『可能性』と『巡ってきた機会』という二つの意味が発達した。
etymology.en: Chance came through Old French cheance, meaning an occurrence, accident, or fortune, from a form related to Latin cadentia and cadere, meaning to fall. It originally referred to something that happens or falls to someone by accident. From this developed both the probability sense and the opportunity sense of a favorable occasion.

nuance.ja: might have＋過去分詞の中心用法は、過去の出来事について確信度の低い可能性を示すこと。He might have missed the train. は、実際に乗り遅れた可能性も、そうでない可能性も残す。if＋過去完了を伴う場合は、実現しなかった過去の可能性を表し、If we had left earlier, we might have caught the train. なら、実際には早く出ず、電車にも乗れなかったことを示唆する。You might have told me! は『言ってくれてもよかったのに』という非難。may have done とほぼ同義だが、might のほうがやや控えめ・不確実に聞こえることがある。
nuance.en: The central use of might have followed by a past participle is to express an uncertain possibility concerning a past event. He might have missed the train leaves open both possibilities. With if plus the past perfect, it describes a counterfactual possible result: If we had left earlier, we might have caught the train normally implies that we did not leave earlier and did not catch it. You might have told me! is a reproach meaning that the person should have said something. May have done is often interchangeable, although might can sound slightly more tentative or uncertain.

ja: He might have left.：彼は帰ったかもしれない。
He might not have left.：彼は帰らなかったかもしれない。
He may have left.：彼は帰ったかもしれない。might とほぼ同義。
He could have left.：彼は帰ることもできた・帰った可能性もある。
He must have left.：彼は帰ったに違いない。
You might have told me!：私に言ってくれてもよかったのに。
We might have won if we had practiced more.：もっと練習していれば、勝てたかもしれない。
en: He might have left expresses an uncertain past possibility.
He might not have left expresses the possibility that he did not leave.
He may have left is nearly equivalent.
He could have left can describe either an available option or a possible explanation.
He must have left expresses a strong inference.
You might have told me! is a reproach.
We might have won if we had practiced more describes a counterfactual possible result.

etymology.ja: might は may の歴史的な過去形で、古英語 meahte・mihte『力があった、可能だった』にさかのぼる。may は能力・可能性を表すゲルマン系の語。might に完了形 have＋過去分詞が続くことで、過去の不確かな可能性や、実現しなかった仮定的結果を表す構文となった。
etymology.en: Might developed historically as the past form of may and goes back to Old English meahte or mihte, meaning had the power or was able. May is a Germanic modal associated with ability and possibility. Combined with the perfect have plus a past participle, might expresses an uncertain past possibility or a possible but unrealized result.

note.ja: ～したかもしれない。推測用法ではほぼ同義だが、might より可能性をわずかに強く感じさせる場合がある。
note.en: A near-equivalent for uncertain past possibility, sometimes perceived as slightly less tentative than might have done.

note.ja: ～した可能性がある、または～することもできた。推測に加えて能力・機会も表す。
note.en: Can express an uncertain past possibility, but also an unused ability, opportunity, or option.

note.ja: ひょっとすると～した。副詞 perhaps を用いた、より直接的な言い換え。
note.en: A direct paraphrase using the adverb perhaps to express uncertainty.

note.ja: ～すべきだった。非難用法では近いが、should のほうが義務・適切さを明確に表す。
note.en: Similar in reproachful contexts, but more explicitly expresses duty or what would have been appropriate.
